case_name: Vikramjeet Singh Chib vs The Union Of India And 2 Ors

parties.respondent_defendant: THE UNION OF INDIA and 2 ORS, REP. BY THE SECY. TO THE GOVT. OF INDIA, MINISTRY OF DEFENCE, NEW DELHI

facts_of_case: Petitioner was a Constable (General duty) in SSB, Rangia. He had matrimonial problems and was facing cases filed by his wife at Jammu. He was required to go on leave due to these issues, but was subsequently denied as he didn't report for duties.

legal_principles.principle: The imposition of two punishments on a person is violative of the principle against double jeopardy.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the authorities has imposed two punishments, namely, punishment of pack drill for 28 days as well as the dismissal from service by the impugned discharge order 28.02.2011, consequently, such action of the respondent authorities as the effect of exposing the petitioner to double jeopardy.
cited_cases: Union of India and others -Vs- Mahammad Ramzan Khan reported in (1991) 1 SCC 588

legal_principles.principle: A person who has already been awarded punishment earlier cannot be subjected to a harsher penalty without just cause.
legal_principles.held: Alternatively, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that since the petitioner has already been awarded punishment earlier, the imposition of penalty of dismissal from service is too harsh to be imposed on the petitioner and as such, the punishment imposed is disproportionate and therefore, should be interfered with and appropriate orders thereon be passed by this court.
cited_cases: Vijay Singh -Vs- Union of India and others reported in (2007) 9 SCC 63
